edges.description: Desmoglein 1 suppresses EGFR-ERK1/2 signalling independently of its adhesive ectodomain, so less desmoglein 1 means less suppression.

edges.description: Fewer, smaller desmosomes cannot hold suprabasal keratinocytes together under load, and the cells separate.

edges.description: Adhesion failure in mechanically stressed palmoplantar skin is followed by hyperkeratosis along lines of stress. The steps between disadhesion and the thickened stratum corneum are not established.
The weight-bearing sole is the most mechanically loaded site and is usually affected first.
Separation of suprabasal keratinocytes is seen on biopsy as acantholysis.
Without enough DSG1-dependent suppression of EGFR-ERK signalling, keratinocytes do not progress normally through terminal differentiation.
edges.source: Reduced DSG1-Dependent Suppression of EGFR-ERK Signaling

edges.description: Disordered terminal differentiation contributes to the thickened palmoplantar epidermis.

nodes.description: SPPK1 palm skin shows perturbed epidermal differentiation: the stress-associated keratin K16 is strongly induced and involucrin labelling is abnormal.

evidence.reference_title: Striate palmoplantar keratoderma arising from desmoplakin and desmoglein 1 mutations is associated with contrasting perturbations of desmosomes and the keratin filament network.
evidence.snippet: In both types of SPPK upregulation of K16 was pronounced and involucrin labelling was abnormal.

nodes.description: On biopsy, widened intercellular spaces and partial acantholysis of spinous keratinocytes distinguish DSG1 keratoderma from other inherited keratodermas.

evidence.reference_title: Disadhesion of epidermal keratinocytes: a histologic clue to palmoplantar keratodermas caused by DSG1 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Widening of the intercellular spaces and disadhesion of epidermal keratinocytes may serve as a histologic clue to PPKs caused by DSG1 mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the desmoglein 1 gene in five Pakistani families with striate palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Mutation analysis resulted in the identification of one recurrent mutation (p.R26X) and four novel mutations (c.Ivs4-2A>G, c.515C>T, c.Ivs9-3C>G, and c.1399delA) in the DSG1 gene. Each mutation is predicted to cause haploinsufficiency of DSG1 protein.

evidence.reference_title: Striate palmoplantar keratoderma resulting from a missense mutation in DSG1.
evidence.snippet: To date, more than 25 mutations in DSG1 have been identified in patients with SPPK1. These mutations were uniformly found to result in a premature termination codon (PTC).

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation in the desmoglein 1 gene underlies striate keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Direct DNA sequencing analysis revealed a heterozygous C-to-A transversion at nt 395 of the DSG1 gene.

evidence.reference_title: Bi-Allelic DSG1 Splice-Site Variant Identified in a Family With Non-Syndromic Striate Palmoplantar Keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: An exon-trap assay confirmed splicing disruption, although some wild-type (WT) transcripts were also detected. The partial retention of DSG1 WT transcripts may explain the mild phenotype.

nodes.description: Heterozygous DSG1 variants introduce a premature termination codon in the extracellular domain or the prosequence (nonsense, single-base insertions or deletions, and splice-site changes that skip an out-of-frame exon). The mutant transcript is expected to be removed by nonsense-mediated decay, and cDNA from affected skin carries no detectable mutant message, so the mutant allele drops out and the disease is caused by haploinsufficiency. An early in-frame exon-skipping splice variant that removes part of the first extracellular domain, and a single missense allele, show that loss of adhesive function without loss of protein can produce the same phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of dominant mutations in the desmosomal cadherin desmoglein 1, causing the skin disease striate palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: All were heterozygotic mutations in the extracellular domain leading to a truncated protein, due either to an addition or deletion of a single base, or a base change resulting in a stop codon.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of dominant mutations in the desmosomal cadherin desmoglein 1, causing the skin disease striate palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: This latter mutation thus results in the mutant allele synthesising only 25 amino acid residues of the prosequence of the protein so that this is effectively a null mutation implying that dominance in the case of this mutation was caused by haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Striate palmoplantar keratoderma resulting from a frameshift mutation in the desmoglein 1 gene.
evidence.snippet: We predict that this mutation will lead to the skipping of exon 12 which is out of frame (134nt), subsequent degradation of the mutant mRNA by non-sense mediated RNA decay, and haploinsufficiency for DSG1.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations in DSG1 causing striate palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Direct sequencing of cDNA derived from affected skin in one patient failed to reveal a pathogenic mutation, suggesting that SPPK results from haploinsufficiency for DSG1.

evidence.reference_title: N-terminal deletion in a desmosomal cadherin causes the autosomal dominant skin disease striate palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: This causes aberrant splicing of exon 2 to exon 4, which are in-frame, with the consequent removal of exon 3 encoding part of the prosequence, the mature protein cleavage site and part of the first extracellular domain.

evidence.reference_title: Striate palmoplantar keratoderma resulting from a missense mutation in DSG1.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we present, to our knowledge, the first case of SPPK caused by a missense (rather than PTC-causing) mutation affecting a residue predicted to be of critical importance for DSG1-mediated adhesion.

nodes.description: Focal hyperkeratosis at weight-bearing sites of the sole (toes, ball and heel), usually appearing in the first years of life before the palmar changes.

nodes.description: Mid and upper spinous keratinocytes separate, with widened intercellular spaces and partial disadhesion that can extend into the granular layer. The palms and soles carry the highest mechanical load and depend most on desmosomal adhesion, which is why the disease is confined to them and is worst at pressure points.

evidence.reference_title: Disadhesion of epidermal keratinocytes: a histologic clue to palmoplantar keratodermas caused by DSG1 mutations.
evidence.snippet: varying degrees of widening of the intercellular spaces and partial disadhesion of keratinocytes in the mid and upper epidermal spinous cell layers, often extending to the granular cell layer.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of dominant mutations in the desmosomal cadherin desmoglein 1, causing the skin disease striate palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: The most severe consequences of SPPK mutations are in regions of the body where pressure and abrasion are greatest and where desmosome function is most necessary.

nodes.description: Desmoglein 1 binds Erbin, which disrupts SHOC2-mediated Ras-Raf scaffolds and so inhibits ERK1/2 activation. This brake on EGFR-ERK signalling lets keratinocytes leaving the basal layer progress through terminal differentiation, and it does not need the adhesive ectodomain. In SPPK1 epidermis Ras-SHOC2 colocalization is increased and Erbin-SHOC2 colocalization is decreased, consistent with the brake being weakened.

evidence.reference_title: Desmoglein-1/Erbin interaction suppresses ERK activation to support epidermal differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Conversely, analysis of epidermis from DSG1-deficient patients with SPPK demonstrated increased Ras-SHOC2 colocalization and decreased Erbin-SHOC2 colocalization, offering a possible explanation for the observed epidermal defects.

evidence.reference_title: Desmoglein-1/Erbin interaction suppresses ERK activation to support epidermal differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Erbin blocks ERK signaling by interacting with and disrupting Ras-Raf scaffolds mediated by SHOC2, a protein genetically linked to the RASopathy, Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair (NS/LAH).

nodes.description: Desmoglein 1 is the principal desmosomal cadherin of the upper epidermis. In DSG1-mutant palm skin, suprabasal desmosomes are fewer and smaller, and the keratins K5, K14 and K10 are reduced, while K16 is induced.

evidence.snippet: The expression of keratins K5, K14 and K10 was reduced in Dsg1-associated SPPK skin, whereas perinuclear aggregation of keratin filaments was more evident in Dp-associated SPPK.

nodes.description: Linear hyperkeratotic bands along the volar surface of each finger, extending onto the palm. Palmar changes usually follow the plantar lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of dominant mutations in the desmosomal cadherin desmoglein 1, causing the skin disease striate palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Recently we have identified a mutation in the DSG1 gene coding for desmoglein 1 as the cause of the autosomal dominant skin disease striate palmoplantar keratoderma (SPPK) in which affected individuals have marked hyperkeratotic bands on the palms and soles.

evidence.reference_title: Striate palmoplantar keratoderma resulting from a frameshift mutation in the desmoglein 1 gene.
evidence.snippet: Clinically, these patients presented with hyperkeratotic palms and with linear hyperkeratosis on the fingers.

nodes.description: Keratolytic preparations (for example urea or salicylic acid in an emollient) and paring of the hyperkeratotic skin are the listed treatment for striate PPK. No trial has been done in SPPK1.
